label: DCN TCP Bridge
info:
Sierra Radio Systems — DCN ↔ TCP Bridge

Bidirectional bridge between one DCN RS-485 serial bus and a single TCP
socket.  No MQTT broker required.

Connection model:
  Python (server, port 4880) ← Node-RED (client, this flow)

A SINGLE TCP connection carries traffic in BOTH directions:
  RS-485 serial IN  → [Validate + Attach Session] → tcp out (reply)
  tcp in (client)   → [Store Session + Route]     → RS-485 serial OUT

The 'tcp in' node opens the connection when Node-RED starts.  Python
sends one CR byte on connect so this node fires immediately and stores
the TCP session.  After that, serial→Python packets are forwarded on
the same socket using 'Reply to TCP' mode.

Setup (single bus):
1. Double-click 'DCN Serial Port' — set your serial port and baud rate.
2. In the 'Connect to Python' tcp in node, set host to the Python
   machine IP and port to match nodered_tcp.port in comms_config.yaml
   (default 4880).
3. Start Python first so the TCP server is listening, then deploy.

Setup (multiple DCN buses):
Import this flow again for each additional bus.  On each new tab:
  a. Set a different serial port and baud rate.
  b. Change the port in the 'Connect to Python' tcp in node (e.g. 4881).
  c. Add a matching bus entry in comms_config.yaml.

Multiple modules on one bus: no changes needed.  The flow forwards all
packets transparently; Python routes to device handlers by address.

name: Validate + Attach Session
Store Session + Route to Serial
RX path — DCN serial → TCP session reply to Python
TX path — TCP from Python (single connection) → DCN serial
